sampling_rule: Every 6th record counting from the first (1-based records 1, 7, 13, 19, ...) in each of ch01, ch09, ch12, ch13, ch14, taken in file order. Record counts in the files: ch01 90, ch09 21, ch12 19, ch13 15, ch14 29, so the sample is ch01 {1,7,...,85} (15), ch09 {1,7,13,19} (4), ch12 {1,7,13,19} (4), ch13 {1,7,13} (3), ch14 {1,7,13,19,25} (5). No file yielded fewer than 3 records, so the 'first 3' fallback was not used. Every sampled record was checked against its stated pdf_page_index (page images read, not text search).
summary_notes: All 31 quotes were found on their stated PDF page. No quote was missing and no page index was off. Quotes match the page word for word, apart from line-break or hyphen handling noted per record.

The 2 'wrong' verdicts are role errors, not quote errors: (a) ch01 Ro 01-6128, where the page says the PAMs 'did not exhibit any agonist activity of their own' yet the record is named 'Agonist'; (b) ch09 aripiprazole, where the page calls the action 'stabilizing' and sets it apart from stimulation (= receptor agonism), yet the record is named 'Receptor Agonist'.

Systematic convention to review: allosteric modulators are mapped to Agonist (PAM) or Antagonist (NAM), and 'inverse agonist' to Antagonist. In this sample the page never uses the words agonist/antagonist for CPCCOEt (NAM), ADX47273 (PAM), MNI-135 (NAM) and the 5-HT2A 'inverse agonists'; these are graded 'correct but inferred'. If the dataset needs the exact book role, these four plus Ro 01-6128 are the affected records (5 of 15 in ch01).

Enzyme 'inducer' mapped to Activator (2 sampled records: ch09 phenobarbital on UDPG transferase, ch12 alcohol on CYP2E1) and 'serotonin reuptake' recorded as a transporter target (ch12 citalopram) are inference steps, graded 'correct but inferred'.

Several sampled records are class statements or nonspecific (no compound: ch01 x3, ch09 ACE, ch14 x2 ; unspecified receptor: ch09 adrenaline, ch14 olanzapine). They match the page but carry little target-level information.
